record.paper: On symmetric intersecting families of vectors

dossier_meta.paper: On symmetric intersecting families of vectors
dossier_meta.catalog_title: Largest symmetric intersecting families are set-intersecting
dossier_meta.statement_text: It seems possible (but maybe impossible to prove) that the largest symmetric intersecting families in $[k]^n$ are set-intersecting.
dossier_meta.context_text: A family $A \subset [k]^n$ is set-intersecting if there exists a symmetric intersecting family $\mathcal{B}$ of subsets of $[n]$ and $\ell \in [k]$ such that $x \in A$ if and only if there is some $B \in \mathcal{B}$ with $x_i = \ell$ for all $i \in B$. The authors note that all their best constructions have this form, motivating the conjecture.
